newsitem.title: LATVIA: ESTONIA FOURTH IN EU ENLARGEMENT LINE - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA FOURTH IN EU ENLARGEMENT LINE - REPORT.

text.p: Estonia is fourth in line among the countries bidding for EU membership with Baltic siblings Latvia and Lithuania further down the list, the newspaper The European Voice said in a recent edition, citing European Commission (EC) sources.

The paper quoted one "EC insider" as saying that none of the candidates from Eastern Europe look to "be in terribly good shape," and that even the front runners will have to wait five or six years before they are admitted into the coveted European club.
The paper said that the Czech Republic is at the head of the pack followed by Slovenia, Hungary and Estonia. Poland, long viewed as a leading candidate, was ranked a surprising fifth.

"Latvia and Lithuania...are also falling behind due to poor law and order and leaky borders. EU administrators point to widespread organised crime and an inability to control trade with Russia as obstacles to their bids for Union membership," the paper said.
But the paper added that "political considerations" could push Estonia further down the list regardless of its economic performance.
It quoted Estonian Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves as saying that efforts to reach EU standards could be scuppered by countries left out of enlargement for the "wrong reasons."
